title: Canonical normalization of completed coefficients and completeness
statement: Let X be any scheme [def-pc-scheme], A a commutative ring, I an ideal, and K an unbounded derived module over adicLisseCompletedRing X I [def-sfb-adic-stratified-perfect-data]. Transport to the small pro-etale site [def-weil-proetale-inverse-image]. There is a canonical isomorphism c from the transported completed ring to ConstantCompletion.completed, commuting with every finite projection through the constant-sheaf comparison [lem-weil-pbc-constant-completion-equivalence]. Define N(K) by termwise transport of the localization representative followed by scalar restriction along c inverse and localization. Then IsSfbAdicComplete X I K if and only if ConstantCompletion.IsComplete at the normalized residue projection holds for N(K). No Noetherianity, boundedness or ideal-generation hypothesis is imposed.

source.place: Proposition 6.6.11 reverse implication, gluing the completeness sentence on finite strata; Lemma 6.5.8(1) and Remark 6.5.10

proof.text: The constant-sheafification comparison for AsSmall.down gives a natural isomorphism on constant commutative rings. Naturality at each quotient transition gives an isomorphism of the positive quotient diagrams. Preservation of limits gives coefficients; the projection formula for the limit isomorphism proves its compatibility with every finite projection.

For a square of residue projections with isomorphisms on source and target rings, their kernel ideals correspond sectionwise: lift a section through the source-ring isomorphism; the target-ring isomorphism is injective, so its image vanishes precisely when the original image does. The ideal generated by the kernel image is exactly the new kernel. The sheaf ideal local-membership axiom identifies its local saturation with itself. Apply restrictScalars_locallyDerivedComplete_iff. Specialize this square to the inverse completed-coefficient comparison and the inverse constant residue comparison. This is exactly the equivalence for N(K).
